T-003 and T-005 (Risk: medium) are correctly non-sensitive per their own Risk Rationale (binding/provenance metadata; cross-epic fixture validation with bounded blast radius). All four Risk: high tasks (T-001, T-002, T-004, T-006; no Risk: critical task exists) carry a 'TDD evidence'/'TDD evidence recorded' Done-When item naming explicit RED (failing test against a deliberately broken component/fixture) and GREEN (full suite against the correct implementation) conditions, plus 'An independent quality-gate verdict records PASS' in every case (T-001 Done When final bullet; T-002 Done When final bullet; T-004 Done When final bullet, which additionally requires confirmation that both human-copy bundles were applied and verified; T-006 Done When final bullet). This satisfies Red→Green capture and an independent-review verdict distinct from the implementing agent, consistent with this repository's standing quality-gate-as-independent-reviewer convention (also reflected in design.md's own 'Impl-Review-Status: Passed' header). No critical-tier task exists, so the second-approver/signed-bundle requirement does not apply.

T-001 (5 work areas: resolver core, suite, fixture tree, ADR-0025, CI registration) and T-004 (6 work areas: 3-state Gate logic, --diagnose, direct risk-gate-matrix.md/SKILL.md edits, Bundle A staging, Bundle B staging, CI registration) each exceed the 3-area oversizing indicator on a naive read, but both carry an explicit 'Note on scope breadth (task-review round 1, TASK-SIZE)' paragraph in tasks.md itself demonstrating this was already raised and resolved: design.md's own Technical Summary, API/Contract Plan, Components table, and Global Constraints ('the new ADR... is drafted and added as PART OF T-001's implementation commit A'; 'T-004 is the sole editor of both' protected-file bundles, to avoid a human-copy staging race across tasks) explicitly bundle these deliverables at the frozen (Impl-Review-Status: Passed) design layer — splitting them would contradict design.md, not merely re-decompose it. Done-When item counts stay within bound (T-001: 6 top-level bullets; T-004: 8 top-level bullets, at but not over the 8-item threshold). No fragmentation indicator is present (no 3+ single-function/file-edit tasks, no bare 'rename X to Y' task) across T-001..T-006. tasks.md is byte-identical to attempt-6/round-1's PASS-bound content on this point; carried as advisory under the provenance re-review convergence rule.

acceptance-tests.md's 'Test Type' column uses domain-specific labels ('glob semantics', 'classification', 'applicability derivation', 'dual-runtime parity (product wrapper direct)', etc.) rather than the literal unit/integration/e2e/acceptance vocabulary, but no declared label contradicts its actual scope: every row is structurally keyed to a specific AC-NNN (the table's own first column), satisfying the acceptance-reference criterion for the whole file; T-006's 'dual-runtime parity (product wrapper direct)' tests (TEST-050/051) explicitly compare exactly two runtime components (the .sh and .ps1 invocation of the same wrapper, per design.md's Canonical normalized stdout JSON form and acceptance-tests.md's own Notes: 'the only cases that invoke both runtimes of a product wrapper... from within a single test process to diff their output directly'), matching an integration-scope test's 'at least two system components' requirement; T-001/T-002's fixture-driven suites each target a single script's classification/collection boundary (resolve-component-paths.py), consistent with a narrow unit/functional scope. No mismatch identified.

All four Risk: high tasks carry an explicit 'Rollback:' field: T-001 ('revert this task's two commits (B then A, or both)... Reverting also removes ADR-0025'); T-002 ('revert this task's two commits; nothing protected is written directly... a revert PR states whether an already-applied test.yml step should be hand-reverted'); T-004 ('revert this task's two commits... The nine staged protected candidates and .github/workflows/test.yml are NEVER part of the agent's own commit history... a revert PR must separately state whether any already-human-applied protected-file change should also be hand-reverted, and by whom'); T-006 ('revert this task's two commits; nothing protected is written directly (a revert PR states whether an already-applied test.yml step should be hand-reverted)'). infra-spec.md's own Rollback section corroborates the same trigger/procedure split between unprotected direct-revert files and protected human-copy-reapplication files.

Shared-file edits are either serialized via Blockers matching Global Constraints' explicit ordering, or are non-conflicting distinct additions: resolve-component-paths.py is edited by T-001→T-002→T-003→T-004 with each downstream task's Blockers covering every upstream editor; tests/run-all.sh/.ps1 and the staged human-copy/.github/workflows/test.yml candidate are edited by T-001→T-002→T-003→T-004→T-006 in the identical Global-Constraints-mandated serialized order, each task's Blockers list covering the full upstream chain; tests/fixtures/component-path-ownership/ is extended by T-001/T-002/T-004/T-005 but each adds distinct new files/subtrees (diff-basis fixtures vs. Fail-1..6 fixtures vs. cross-epic seed fixtures), not the same file for the same purpose. CHANGELOG.md is edited by all six tasks, but Global Constraints require each task to land its OWN new '## Unreleased' block ('never an append to another task's entry') and mandate 'implement one task at a time' — T-002 and T-005 (both blocked only on T-001, so nominally schedulable in parallel) do not share a Blockers edge, but the one-task-at-a-time execution constraint removes the concurrent-write risk this check targets. No two tasks claim the same protected file: guard-invariants.json+siblings and check-contract.*/risk-gate-matrix.md are each named 'T-004 is the sole editor' in Global Constraints.

Every Blockers edge maps to a disclosed functional or shared-resource dependency, and the task text is explicit where a blocker is purely a serialization concern rather than a functional one: T-004's Blockers include T-003, and its own Depends On text states plainly 'T-003 is not a functional dependency — the Gate's Fail conditions do not consume ownership_digest,' attributing the blocker instead to the shared tests/run-all.sh/.ps1 array and .github/workflows/test.yml single-writer staging constraint Global Constraints establish — a genuine shared-resource dependency, not a fabricated one. T-003's Blockers on T-002 is grounded in both tasks incrementally extending the same resolve-component-paths.py invocation/output shape ('emitted on the same resolve invocation T-002 completes'). T-006's Blockers on T-001/T-002/T-003/T-004 match its own stated need for both product wrapper pairs to be functionally complete before parity-testing them. No task's scope depends on another's output without a declared Blocker: T-005 (cross-epic fixture, classification-only) correctly declares only T-001, not T-002/T-003/T-004, consistent with its scope never touching the git-diff collector, digest emitter, or Gate.

SKIP: no bugfix or debugging task in scope. T-001..T-006 are all greenfield build-out tasks for Epic A3 (Component Path Ownership) — none is scoped as a bugfix, regression fix, debugging session, flaky-test resolution, or incident remediation by title, Goal, Scope, or Done When text.
